walkthroughs.body_html:
Thermodynamics — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Thermodynamics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Thermodynamics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which species has the same electron configuration as Ar?
options: Na⁺
Cl⁻
F⁻
Mg²⁺

mcqs.q: Successive ionisation energies of an atom always:
options: Decrease
Stay the same
Increase
Vary randomly

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.
Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.
Entropy measures how much energy a system contains in total.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
Entropy measures how much energy a system contains in total.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.

mcqs.q: What does an increase in entropy of a system correspond to?
options: An increase in the number of ways energy and particles can be arranged — typically a more dispersed/'disordered' state.
Entropy is just a measure of how messy a system looks visually.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Entropy measures how much energy a system contains in total.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ionisation energy”?
options: Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Relative atomic mass”?
options: Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Isotope”?
options: Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Mass number A”?
options: Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Atomic number Z”?
options: Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
Distribution of electrons across s, p, d and f subshells, filling lowest energy first.
Weighted mean mass of an atom relative to 1/12 of the mass of a ¹²C atom.
Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
